punchline: Susan Jeffers argues that blaming yourself isn't taking responsibility at all; it's just another way of playing the victim.
thirty_sec: Susan Jeffers, in Feel the Fear and Do It Anyway, says a lot of fear lives in how we talk. So she offers a swap list. 'I can't' becomes 'I won't.' 'I should' becomes 'I could.' 'It's terrible' becomes 'It's a learning experience.' Same situation, different speaker in charge. And her twist on responsibility: it means not blaming others, but also not blaming yourself, because self-blame keeps you just as stuck.
question: Is there something you tell people you 'can't' do that's really something you've decided not to do?
